qualitative.gate_3m_moat_note: AIG benefits from global multinational licensing, balance sheet capacity, and broker distribution for complex commercial risks. However, empirical proof of moat fails decisively: 10-year median ROIC of 7.5% and GAAP ROE of 7.5-8.6% fall well short of the 12% hurdle. Commercial P&C pricing is governed by cyclical market hard/soft dynamics rather than persistent structural pricing power, while broker intermediation (Marsh, Aon) and aggressive competition from peers (Chubb, Travelers, Zurich) arbitrage away excess returns.
qualitative.note: Fails Gate 3b (ROIC < 12%, REJECT). Despite successful portfolio simplification under Peter Zaffino—culminating in the full separation and exit from Corebridge Financial by 2026—AIG remains a cyclical commercial P&C insurer. A 10-year median ROIC of 7.5% and recent ROIC of 5.0-7.5% fail the 12% hurdle rate. Underwriting profits remain subject to casualty social inflation, catastrophe volatility, and the broader commercial insurance pricing cycle rather than an enduring competitive moat.
qualitative.evidence: 10-year median ROIC is 7.5%, with 2023-2025 ROIC hovering between 4.3% and 7.5%. GAAP ROE reached 8.6% in 2023 and 7.5% in 2025 (Core Operating ROE ~11.1%), failing the 12% multi-cycle hurdle. While General Insurance calendar combined ratio improved to 90.1%-92.9% and ex-CAT AYCR to ~88%, commercial lines lack persistent pricing power above inflation due to broker shopping (Marsh, Aon) and deep capacity from rival carriers. Successful execution of Corebridge (CRBG) sell-down through the Nippon Life deal and 2026 final exit simplified the corporate structure but does not lift baseline economic returns above cost of capital.
